alejandra: Anybody else seeing a p99 spike out of CDG around 08:15 UTC? Grafana shows a sharp jump + kernel-selector flip. https://grafana/redwood/d/serving/cdg-pop

sourabh: Yup. Noticed a multipath reshuffle from the upstream provider at 08:12. traceroute showed two equal-cost paths, one added ~12ms extra RTT.

sourabh: traceroute snippet:
```
traceroute to 10.4.3.2 (10.4.3.2), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.1.0.1  0.62 ms  0.59 ms  0.56 ms
 2  * * *
 3  83.189.0.1  6.1 ms  6.0 ms  6.2 ms
 4  62.210.0.1  18.3 ms  18.6 ms  18.2 ms <-- alternate path appeared
```

maria_g: did a quick perf sample on an affected host. flamegraph shows a notable shift: kernel_selector.choose_safe() spikes when path RTT > selector_threshold (~10ms). continuous_batcher waits more often and kvcache warmups fail.

maria_g: perf top lines:
```
30.2%  kernel_selector::choose_safe()
18.7%  continuous_batcher::wait_for_batch()
12.4%  memcpy
10.0%  gpu_sync
```

kevin: So the upstream RTT bump pushed us over the kernel-selector boundary, which picks a conservative kernel that disables some batching/KV coalescing optimizations. That explains both p99 and throughput drop. :thinking_face:

alejandra: Can we confirm which kernel flags flip? Which config is effectively toggled?

maria_g: The safe kernel toggles: disable_continuous_batching=true, kv_cache_coalesce=off, affinity_hint=legacy. Logs show "kernel_switch: fast->safe (cause=rtt_threshold)" at 08:12:19

kevin: I can force the kernel back to fast-path for CDG at the routing level or override selector for the POP. Quick mitigation: set runtime.override_kernel=fast-path for pop=cdg. Will do if y'all agree.

alejandra: Do it. Also reduce max_batch_wait to 10ms to avoid batching stalls while we investigate.

oncall-bot: deploy triggered by kevin: infra/configs/runtime/cdg/override_kernel=fast-path (change-id: cfg-3579)

kevin: Applied override and bumped max_batch_wait -> 10ms. Observing metrics...

maria_g: p99 dropped back to baseline within ~3m. continuous_batcher queue depth normalized, kvcache hit-rate recovered as coalescing resumed. Recorded traces:
```
p99 before override: 290ms
p99 after override: 78ms
kvcache_hit_ratio before: 0.62
kvcache_hit_ratio after: 0.93
```

alejandra: Nice. We still need a proper postmortem: root cause appears to be upstream multipath reshuffle that nudged RTT over our selector threshold. Action items:
- sourabh: collect BGP/peering logs for provider and file ticket with them (owner)
- maria_g: run controlled perf tests to reproduce threshold behavior and capture a full flamegraph (owner)
- kevin: add a temporary automation to detect small RTT shifts and avoid immediate kernel flip if throughput/kv metrics drop (owner)

sourabh: filing with provider now plus exporting pcap/traceroutes from affected hosts.

kevin: For longer-term: we should change kernel_selector to consider kvcache hit-rate and batching queue depth, not just RTT. Opened infra issue: https://issues/redwood/INF-2418

alejandra: Thanks team. I'll schedule a 30m postmortem tomorrow 09:30 UTC to capture findings and decide on selector changes. :spiral_note_pad:

maria_g: adding collected perf samples and flamegraphs to the incident ticket.

kevin: leaving the override in place for 24h while provider responds. Will roll back if no regression.

alejandra: closing thread for now, please update the incident doc when you have artifacts. :white_check_mark:
